doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: Closing remarks on Houston Person and the cruise
summary: She praises Houston, who finds her work, and they wrap up with talk of birthdays and the cruise.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well it’s really been a pleasure talking with you and I—
I loved it.
I haven’t asked you — anything that you’d like to add?
It’s easy talking to you. Sometimes when I get started, you know, you’ve got to shut me up.
It doesn’t sound like that you guys have too much trouble finding work these days, you’re working a lot.
No. If there’s a job anywhere, Houston will find it.
Well it’s nice to have someone taking care of that end of the business.

When we started working together, that was really wonderful for me, because I don’t have to worry about a thing. He’s like my brother, my father, my husband, only he’s not my husband. People say, “Are they married?” I say, “Yeah we’re married but to two different people.” Because they’ve married us all over the country. But he’s wonderful, he’s been very good for me, and I hope I’ve been good for him.
I think so. I could tell.
Thank you.
Well it’s been a great pleasure and I wish you the best for both of your birthdays coming up, and I hope you have a great cruise.
Thank you so much. Are you going to be on this cruise?
I don’t think so. Tim, can we go on this cruise? That was a slice of heaven. I mean I have to tell you that I agreed with you, it was like being in another world.
That’s what it is.
Just going from room to room and hearing all these great artists.
And having people cut your lettuce up. I mean—
Something to look forward to.
It was very nice Monk, I enjoyed talking with you.
Thank you so much.
And thank you too.
All right.
